_provenance.transcription_method: All 38 d-TPP records of PHL were downloaded to raw/kphl_dtpp_2610_pdfs/, their text layers extracted with pdfjs-dist (raw/kphl_dtpp_2610_txt/) and every chart marked 'transcribed' below was rendered (pdftoppm 240 dpi, the airport diagram 450 dpi) and read visually. Per transcription: the airport diagram 00320AD.PDF (taxiway identifiers, charted headings, frequencies, hot spots, pavement strength); ILS/LOC and RNAV (GPS) plates 00320IL9L, IL26, IL27L, IL27R, IZL17, IZLZ9R, IV9RCON, IV17CON, R17, R26, R27L, R27R, R35, RY9L, RY9R (fixes and roles, minima, missed approach, plate notes); 00320PHILADELPHIA(_C) (DP); 00320BOJID and 00320PAATS(_C) (STARs); NE4HOTSPOT.PDF (hot-spot text). Special-authorization, CAT II/III, RNP and visual charts are listed with TCH/missed approach from the text layer only.

primary_navaid_note: KPHL has no VOR/DME of its own: the only on-field NASR navaid is PHL VOT 109.8 (VOR test facility, 39.86528 N 75.23365 W), which is not a navigation aid. OOD (WOODSTOWN VORTAC 112.8, chan 75X, 39.63607752 N 75.30305627 W, NJ, OPERATIONAL RESTRICTED) is the VORTAC named as the missed approach hold of most KPHL ILS/RNAV plates and is used as the primary navaid.
ils_note: Six ILS/LOC systems with DME at KPHL (NASR ILS_BASE): runway 9L I-VII 108.95 (CAT I), 9R I-PHL 109.3 (CAT IIIB), 17 I-MYY 108.75 (CAT I, OPERATIONAL RESTRICTED), 26 I-LLH 111.55 (CAT I, localizer offset), 27L I-GLC 109.3 (CAT I), 27R I-PDP 108.95 (CAT I). Runway 35 and runway 8 have no ILS or LOC. The plates call 9L/27R I-VII/I-PDP and 9R/27L I-PHL/I-GLC; each pair shares a frequency (interlocked at opposite ends of one runway).
navaid_unverified: Some approach intersections (QWEST, OBEKE, ANNET, LANDI, MRTIN, HADNI...) are ILS DME fixes; their NASR coordinates are used as published and were not compared with the plate geometry beyond the printed distances.

With no published crossing altitudes the simulator's descend-via clearance has nothing to fly and the controller descends the aircraft by ordinary altitude assignments. Every runway route ends 'then on track/heading N ... Expect RADAR vectors to final approach course' (kept in `narrative`); no `then_heading_mag_deg` is set so that, as for KMHT's runway legs that have an approach, the simulator continues from the last published fix over the plate's join fixes (`join_approach_fixes`) and the controller clears the approach there.

stars_note: Six STARs (seven PDF pages) are published for KPHL: BOJID FOUR, BUNTS THREE, JIIMS FOUR, PAATS FOUR (two pages), SLATT SIX, SPUDS SEVEN. BOJID FOUR and PAATS FOUR are transcribed in full (transitions, runway legs, legs with track and distance, notes). Selection: PAATS FOUR is the only RNAV STAR (with JIIMS FOUR) whose NASR bodies serve every landing runway (9L, 9R, 17, 26, 27L, 27R, 35) and has three transitions from the south and southwest; BOJID FOUR is the RNAV STAR of the west (Harrisburg) corridor serving the 9L/R and 27L/R pairs. No official usage statistic by STAR was found (searched 2026-10-21: phl.org Noise Office, FAA documents, search results); a flight-simulation forum post calls BOJID1 'probably the most used arrival' (anecdotal, not a source), so the choice rests on runway coverage and flow geometry, not measured use.
